note: Houston is the toughest week one draw any elite quarterback got and it does not matter. Allen runs, Allen throws, Allen finishes as the QB1 more weeks than not. Start him and stop thinking about it.
Indianapolis has to account for Henry first and that is exactly the problem. Lamar picks apart whatever is left over, and the rushing floor keeps him locked in at the top of the position.
The whole Cincinnati offense is a buy this week and Burrow is the engine. Expect a high scoring game in Tampa Bay and expect him to throw it plenty.
A divisional opener against Washington always gets ugly, and Hurts wins ugly games with his legs. Expect goalline work nobody else at the position gets.
The other side of that same divisional slugfest. Daniels is the rare young quarterback whose floor is built on rushing, so a rough passing day still pays out.
Carolina is the friendliest matchup on the board for a quarterback trying to prove the leap is real. Expect Williams to push it to Burden and Odunze early and often.

I love what Maye is building with AJ Brown and Seattle is a nasty first assignment. Consensus has him a tier too high and that is a week too early. Expect the connection to be real and the box score to be modest.
Herbert has the arm and now he has the receivers to go with it. Arizona gives up enough through the air to make this a comfortable start.
Cleveland's front is still the best thing about that team and Lawrence has never loved pressure. Fine as a low end starter, nothing more.
Two elite receivers and a divisional matchup he has feasted on for years. Expect Dak to spread it around and put up a clean line.
Purdy is only as good as the room around him, and this one is stocked. A divisional game caps the ceiling but the floor is solid.
Kansas City in week one is a rough draw for a quarterback who needs structure. Startable in deeper formats and nowhere else.
Dart against a Dallas defense that gives up yards in bunches. Expect volume, expect a mistake or two, and expect the line to swing either way.
I have him lower than most and it probably is too low, but that offense has not looked like itself and Denver's defense is real. I need to see it before I move him back up.
Mayfield gets the other half of the Cincinnati shootout and nobody is talking about it. Consensus has him buried. Expect him to throw forty times and make that look silly.
New Orleans is exactly the kind of defense Goff carves up. The Amon-Ra connection does the heavy lifting and the rest takes care of itself.
Stafford still has the arm for the deep shots and now he has Nacua and Adams to throw them to. San Francisco keeps this from being a smash spot.
All eyes are on the Kyler and Jefferson connection and I need a week before I believe in it. Green Bay is a bad place to debut a new partnership.
Darnold has been written off twice and keeps producing anyway. Where consensus has him is disrespectful for a starter with this receiver room. Expect a quietly useful line.
Love has the talent and not the consistency, and a divisional game against Minnesota is where that shows up.
It is now or never for Stroud and Nico Collins and I think they come out firing in Buffalo. Chasing points is good for quarterback production.
Baltimore forces you to throw and Jones has weapons for the first time in a while. Garbage time counts the same in fantasy.
Detroit is going to be ahead early and Shough is going to be throwing into a bad script all afternoon. Consensus is too high on him.
Willis is a runner first and Miami has not shown me a passing structure worth trusting. Consensus is being generous.
Ward against the Jets is the kind of matchup that produces a quiet fifteen points. Fine in superflex, nowhere else.
Cousins has Brock Bowers and a Miami defense that gives up completions. Having him this far down is a mistake for a starting quarterback with a tight end like that. Expect volume.
Rodgers still gets it out fast and Atlanta's secondary is a get right spot. Streamable in a pinch.
Young has flashed and gone quiet more times than I can count. Chicago is not the week to talk yourself into him again.
The quarterback room in Atlanta is a mess and Tua is the one who came out of it with the job. Drake London makes any quarterback usable. Low ceiling, workable floor.
Brissett keeps the lights on and not much else. McBride and Harrison make him watchable, the Chargers make him unstartable.
Geno with the Jets is a hard sell in any format. Garrett Wilson deserves better than this.
Nothing about this profile says start him. Jacksonville is soft enough to keep him on the board in the deepest leagues only.
Backing up Cousins means backing up Cousins. Nothing here until something changes.
Purdy's backup. Not a fantasy asset this week.
The tools have always been there and the job is not. Behind Daniel Jones he is a handcuff, not a start.
Last man on the board for a reason.
Gibbs versus a Saints team trying to find their identity. This is the first edition of Sonic with his training wheels off. Easy RB1.
Everyone's early pick for RB1. I like him over the season but he's going against a solid Steelers defense. He'll do great but fall behind top RB numbers for Week 1.
Best weapon on the Colts against a Ravens team that struggled on the D-line last year. If Madubuike plays to his former form expect slightly lower performance, but overall still a top-tier starter.

I like the Bills reliable runner to have a premier role against the stout Texans defense. Expect his performance to continue to peak throughout the year while losing some close goalline touches to the running prowess of Josh Allen.
Saquon's performance dropoff has a lot of doubters putting him lower in the consensus RB rankings. Don't believe them.
If he can avoid injury the speedster will have perpetual performance gains as the reliable option in a retooled Miami team.
Buy every part of the Bengals high powered offense.
CMC loses a bit of performance against one of the best defenses in the league. Aaron Donald sitting out in Australia gives him some more space in a crowded D-line.
Downhill running with a new offensive scheme and threats, expect him to explode against the colts.
Expect the defending super bowl MVP to get major usage against a tough defensive scheme.
Hype surrounds Hampton and he has a good matchup. Role with a solid low tier RB1.
Despite a few lackluster seasons, Breece Hall has big point potential against a team searching for a change. Expect him to get fed.
Jeanty is going to be a star and Miami is a fine place to start. Consensus is close enough, I just like a couple of the veterans ahead of him for one week.
Kyren keeps getting doubted and keeps getting the ball inside the five. Corum is the talent, Kyren is the workload. Expect touchdowns.
Javonte has the backfield to himself in Dallas and the Giants are a good place to have it. Expect a heavy touch count.
Love has the burst and Arizona has three backs. The Chargers front makes this a tough first look, so consensus is a touch high.
Etienne is fast and New Orleans is going to be behind, which means passing down work. Kamara is still lurking though. Flex play.
Carolina is the matchup you want for a back with Swift's profile. Monangai will steal carries but Swift is the passing down back and that is where the points are.
Irving in a shootout is exactly where you want him. Tampa Bay will be throwing and he catches plenty of them.
Montgomery is the goalline back and Buffalo is a hard place to score. Touchdown dependent, but the touchdowns come.
Price has looked like the most explosive back in that Seattle room and consensus has not caught up. Expect the role to grow fast.
Skattebo runs angry and Dallas invites exactly that. Tracy is going to take snaps, which caps the whole thing.
Tuten has the speed to break a long one on anybody. Cleveland's front means that is the only way he scores.
Judkins is the best back on that roster and the offense around him is the problem. Volume without much efficiency.
Stevenson gets a bigger role this week than people expect. Seattle is stout but the touches will be there.
Warren and Dowdle is a real committee and neither one gets enough for comfort. Atlanta is a good matchup for whoever gets the ball.
Pollard still has juice and the Jets are a fine matchup. Spears eats into the passing work.
The other half of the Pittsburgh committee. Dowdle has been the more efficient one and Warren gets the goalline. Frustrating for both.
Brooks has the talent and Hubbard has the trust. Chicago is a bad matchup to sort that out.
Harvey is the change of pace and Kansas City is a hard place to find space. Deep league flex.
Hubbard keeps outproducing the guy drafted to replace him. Chicago is tough but the touches are real.
Gainwell catches passes in a game that will have plenty of them. PPR only.
Dobbins has been productive whenever healthy and that has always been the whole problem. Kansas City is not the week.
With Jacobs where I have him, Lloyd is more interesting than his ranking. Still a stash for now.
White is the pass catching half of the Washington backfield. A divisional game keeps everyone in check.
Monangai has earned real carries and Carolina is the softest run matchup on the board. Consensus is asleep on him.
Mason is the early down back in a three man room. Green Bay makes that hard to use.
Everyone has moved on from Kamara and the receiving work is still there. Consensus has him far too low for a back who catches this many passes in a losing script. Expect him to matter.
Croskey-Merritt has flashed and the Washington backfield is crowded. Wait and see.
Jones against his old team is a fun story and a bad fantasy start. Three backs is too many.
Corum is the more talented back and Kyren is the one getting the ball. Consensus is buying a role that does not exist yet.
Marks is the receiving back behind Montgomery, and Buffalo means throwing. Deep league flex.
Rodriguez is the short yardage back in Jacksonville. That is a real job even if it is not a fun one.
Three backs in Arizona and Allgeier is the between the tackles one. Hard to trust.
Spears has the ability and Pollard has the workload. Handcuff.
Sampson is behind Judkins on an offense that struggles to score. Bench.
Bigsby is the Barkley handcuff, which is one of the more valuable bench spots in fantasy. Not a start.
Hill is the passing down back in an offense that scores constantly. Consensus ignores what that is worth in PPR. Expect catches.
Vidal has looked good whenever he has played and Hampton cannot take every snap. Worth more than consensus gives him.
Tracy splits with Skattebo and neither one is startable. Dallas is a fine matchup for whoever wins the job.
Behind Walker in Kansas City. Stash only.
Davis is the Cook handcuff on a great offense. That is the whole appeal.
Behind McCaffrey, which means nothing until it means everything. Handcuff.
Wright has the speed and Achane has the job. Stash.
Perine catches passes on a great offense. Deep PPR only.
Third back in a three back room. No thanks.
Fullback. Not a fantasy play.
Blocking back. Nothing here.
This is my biggest call of the week and I will own it. Something is off in Green Bay and I do not trust the workload at all right now. Consensus is still far too high on him for me.
Joe's number one target makes miracles happen. They won't be needed against Tampa Bay, but expect a high scoring game with lots of fantasy potential.
Tons of targets, tons of hype, tons of opportunity
Detroit will have their way with New Orleans, expect the Goff connection to continue for an above average performance for Amon-Ra
Expect glue like coverage from a tough secondary in New England, but JSN will find a way to crack the top 5 nonetheless.
Expect Dak to feed both his receivers. Pickens will pull some targets, but great things are in Ceedee's future.
All eyes are on the Kyler-Jefferson connection. He hasn't performed the same since Kirk and Darnold left the building.
I believe the AJ Brown Drake Maye connection will be real from day one. Get in on the hype early.
It's now or never for the CJ Stroud and Nico Collins connection. I think they get off to a strong start in Buffalo.
Distraction and turnover in the quarterback room throws some questions at Drake London, but with Bijan in the backfield, I expect plenty of opportunities to hit Tua's number one target.

With AJ Brown gone DeVonta Smith just become the only alpha in town. It's put up or shut up time and a divisional matchup against the Commanders is the time to demonstrate how he can carry the offense without other elite talent at wideout.

Another year of George Pickens showing what he can do when he has a good quarterback under center. WR1 talent in a WR2 role. I expect him to pop off against the Giants in an early season primetime game.

High target volume is the right place to live for Rashee Rice against a stout Broncos defense. Injuries have hurt the chiefs the past few seasons, but Rice will continue his onfield performance in game one against the Broncos.
Flowers is the number one in Baltimore and Indianapolis has trouble with speed. Expect Lamar to look his way early and often.
Olave is talented and the quarterback situation is the ceiling. Consensus is paying for the name, and Detroit is not the matchup that fixes it.
Wilson deserves so much better than this quarterback room and produces anyway. Tennessee is a get right spot. Start him.
Nabers is a monster and Dart is still figuring it out. Consensus is fair for the season and a touch high for week one.
Waddle and Nix is a brand new connection and Kansas City is a bad first test. The talent keeps him startable anyway.
Buy the whole Cincinnati offense, and Higgins is the part people forget about. A shootout in Tampa Bay means two receivers eat, not one.
McConkey is Herbert's favorite target and Arizona gives up slot production. Reliable.
Adams is still one of the best route runners alive and Stafford still throws it there. Where consensus has him is a name discount. Expect touchdowns.
Moore with Josh Allen is the kind of upgrade the rankings have not priced in yet. Consensus is too low. Get in early.
McMillan has the size and Bryce Young has the questions. Chicago's secondary is real, so consensus is optimistic.
McLaurin has produced through every quarterback situation imaginable. Philadelphia is tough but he is always involved.
Egbuka is going to be good and Godwin is still there. A shootout helps, but consensus assumes a target share he has not earned yet.
Burden has the juice and Chicago has three receivers to feed. Carolina is a great matchup, I just want to see the target share first.
Washington has quietly become Lawrence's most trusted target. Cleveland is tough but the volume is real.
Williams is a big play waiting to happen and New Orleans gives up chunks. Boom or bust as always.
Watson has the speed and Green Bay spreads it around too much to trust anybody. Divisional games make that worse.
Odunze against Carolina is a fine flex play. Burden's arrival makes the target math harder.
Thomas is the most talented receiver on that roster and consensus has him too low. Cleveland is tough. He is still the guy.
Evans in San Francisco is one of the stranger sights of the offseason. The red zone ability travels, the divisional matchup caps it.
The talent has never been the question and the quarterback play has. Brissett keeps the ceiling low.
Godwin in a shootout is useful. Egbuka taking targets is the risk.
Metcalf with Rodgers should work and Atlanta cannot cover him. Touchdown upside every week.
Pittman joining Metcalf in Pittsburgh makes both of them harder to trust. Atlanta is soft enough for both to matter.
Tate is a name I like long term and consensus is way ahead of the role. Three receivers in Tennessee is too many.
Johnston has finally started catching what is thrown at him. Consensus is too low for the second option on this offense.
Robinson gets volume and no yards after the catch. PPR only.
Sutton is the possession guy and Waddle is the new toy. Kansas City is hard on both.
Wilson is the second option behind Harrison and the quarterback is the problem. Bench.
Downs works the middle and Baltimore takes that away. Too many mouths in Indianapolis anyway.
Diggs still gets open and McLaurin is the alpha. A divisional matchup keeps it modest.
Pierce is a deep threat and nothing else. Boom or bust in the worst way.
Reed is the most useful of the Green Bay receivers, which is not saying much. Bench.
Lemon has a real chance to matter with AJ Brown gone. Not week one though.
Concepcion has flashed and the offense is the ceiling. Watch, do not start.
Addison behind Jefferson with Kyler throwing is a wait and see. Green Bay is a bad debut.
Deebo back in San Francisco is my favorite value on this board. Consensus forgot what he does with the ball in his hands. Expect touches everywhere.
Meyers is reliable and third in line. Deep league only.
Third receiver in San Francisco behind Evans and Deebo. Nothing yet.
Worthy has the speed to change a game and Rice takes the volume. Consensus is too low for a Mahomes receiver.
Shakir is Allen's safety valve and DJ Moore just took the top of that depth chart. Houston is tough.
Another Green Bay receiver in a rotation nobody can predict. Pass.
Coker has earned snaps and Carolina cannot throw. Bench.
Doubs is the second option behind AJ Brown and Seattle is stingy. No.
Jeudy still gets separation and the quarterback play buries him. Consensus was too harsh.
Shaheed is a deep threat on a team with JSN and Kupp. Too many mouths.
Mitchell has the tools and no quarterback. Right matchup, wrong situation.
Jennings is a tough possession receiver behind Jefferson and Addison. Deep leagues only.
Wicks is depth in Philadelphia. Nothing here.
Third receiver on the Jets. Hard pass.
Harris is behind McConkey and Johnston. Watch list.
Tucker gets the speed targets and Bowers takes everything that matters. Consensus was too high.
Lane has size and Lamar throws touchdowns to whoever is open in the red zone. Consensus is too low for that.
Washington works underneath in an offense with no quarterback answer. Bench.
Kupp is not done and consensus was disrespectful. JSN is the alpha, but Darnold trusts veterans. Expect chains moved.
Nailor is the second receiver in a tight end offense. No.
Depth in Miami. Nothing.
Allen is a pro and Indianapolis has too many receivers. Consensus was generous.
Ridley has been passed by Tate and Robinson. Hard to see the path.
Third in Denver behind Waddle and Sutton. Bench.
Mooney is the deep threat behind Nabers, and Dallas gives up big plays. There is a lottery ticket here.
Vele is big and the offense is bad. No.
Coleman has the size and Buffalo just added DJ Moore. That is the whole story.
Bateman has been the same player for years. Flowers and Lane are ahead of him now.
Fourth option in Kansas City. Nothing.
Legette is behind McMillan and Coker. Pass.
Slayton is depth on a team with one real receiver. No.
Douglas works the slot and Seattle covers the slot. Bench.
Last man on the board. Nothing here this week.
McBride is the safest tight end in football because the target share does not move no matter who is throwing. Expect ten looks and a locked in finish.
Bowers is the entire Las Vegas passing game and Cousins is going to lean on him. Miami gives up work over the middle. Expect a big number.
Carolina is the softest matchup on the tight end board and Loveland has grown into the role. Expect Caleb to find him in the red zone.
Kraft has quietly become Love's most reliable target. Divisional games get ugly and ugly games funnel to the tight end.
Warren is going to be very good and Baltimore is a rough introduction. Consensus is a half step early.
Every year we do this with Pitts and every year the talent is undeniable. With the quarterback room in flux he might finally be the safety valve. Expect targets.
Kittle is still the best all around tight end alive when he is on the field and consensus forgets that. Expect him to matter in a divisional game.
New Orleans cannot cover tight ends and Goff knows exactly where LaPorta is going to be. Solid start.
Fannin has real ability and the Cleveland offense is the problem, not him. Consensus is asking a lot from this passing game.
Houston is tough and Buffalo spreads it around, but Allen has always trusted his tight end near the goal line. Touchdown dependent.
Kelce is not what he was and Denver is exactly the defense that exposes it. I need a big game before I put him back in the top ten.
Likely finally gets a room where he is the guy, and Dallas gives up plenty over the middle. Sneaky start.
Everyone has written Andrews off and Lamar keeps throwing him touchdowns. Consensus is too low for a red zone weapon in this offense.
Goedert is useful when healthy and that offense runs through everyone but the tight end. Matchup dependent streamer.
Lamb and Pickens eat first and Ferguson gets what is left. Against the Giants that is still enough.
Johnson is the closest thing New Orleans has to a reliable target. Detroit is a bad matchup and the volume comes anyway in a losing script.
Kyler needs a security blanket in a new offense and Hockenson is the obvious one. Consensus is way off. Expect a lot of work early.
Schultz is Stroud's short yardage answer and Buffalo will force Houston to throw. Streamable.
Strange has the role and Cleveland makes it hard to do anything with it. Bench in most formats.
Okonkwo can win with speed and Washington throws to everybody. A divisional game keeps the ceiling in check.
Henry is Maye's safety valve and that matters against a Seattle defense that takes away the outside. Touchdown or bust.
Dulcich has always had the athleticism and never the opportunity. Miami might finally give it to him. Worth a dart throw.
Barner gets goalline work and not much else. New England makes even that hard.
Helm is on the field and that is about all I can say for him this week.
Engram is a slot receiver wearing a tight end label and Denver needs playmakers. Consensus is low on him, and chasing Kansas City means throwing.
Rodgers has always loved a tight end and Atlanta cannot cover them. That makes Freiermuth a live streamer in deeper leagues.
Otton gets targets when Tampa Bay is chasing, and they will be chasing. Deep league only.
Njoku in a new offense with Herbert is interesting later in the season. Not yet.
Nacua and Adams take every meaningful target. Nothing here.
Taylor will matter eventually. Not with this quarterback situation.
The Bengals offense is a buy and the tight end is the last mouth fed. Bench.
Likely is the tight end in New York now. Johnson is an afterthought.
Loveland took this job and is not giving it back. Kmet blocks and catches the occasional touchdown.
Behind Juwan Johnson on a bad offense. No.
Tremble blocks. That is the note.
Kraft is the guy in Green Bay. Jonnu is depth.
